description: Intrinsic electrochemical stability window (ESW) of comp1 (LPSCl) vs modelc (LPSCl1.6) from the grand-potential phase-diagram method (Mo/Ong/Ceder 2012). Real ESW (Li reservoir opened, μ_Li scanned) — NOT the qualitative competing-phase-span hint from tools/doping/esw_check.py.

method.approach: pymatgen PhaseDiagram.get_element_profile(Li, composition) over the MP GGA_GGA+U corrected Li-P-S-Cl convex hull (108 entries). Needs only the COMPOSITION + MP hull, so comp1 (in MP) and modelc (Li5.4PS4.4Cl1.6, non-stoichiometric, NOT in MP) are handled on identical footing.
method.voltage_convention: V (vs Li/Li+) = mu_Li(metal) - mu_Li ; e=1; 0 V = Li metal. evolution>0 = Li taken up (reduction); evolution<0 = Li released (oxidation); evolution~0 = neutral self-decomposition at OCV.
method.mp_thermo_type: GGA_GGA+U (pinned; avoids R2SCAN mixing noise, matches Mo/Ong literature numbers)

key_breakpoints_V.0.00: Li6PS5Cl + 8 Li -> Li3P + 5 Li2S + LiCl (full reduction at Li metal)
key_breakpoints_V.1.72: Li6PS5Cl -> Li3PS4 + Li2S + LiCl (neutral, no Li flux)
key_breakpoints_V.2.14: -> Li3PS4 + 0.25 LiS4 + LiCl + 1.75 Li (S2- -> polysulfide, FIRST oxidation)
key_breakpoints_V.3.33: -> 0.5 P2S7 + 0.5 S + SCl + 6 Li (Cl oxidation finally)

key_breakpoints_V.2.14: -> Li3PS4 + 0.1 LiS4 + 1.6 LiCl + 0.7 Li (S2- -> polysulfide, FIRST oxidation)
key_breakpoints_V.3.39: -> 0.4588 P2S7 + 0.08235 PCl5 + 1.188 SCl + 5.4 Li (Cl oxidation: SCl + PCl5)

comparison_and_interpretation.headline: comp1 and modelc have essentially IDENTICAL intrinsic ESW (reduction ~1.2-1.7 V, OCV self-decomposition 1.72 V, oxidation onset 2.14 V). Cl-enrichment does NOT improve the oxidation limit because oxidation is S2- -> polysulfide LIMITED in both — S2- oxidizes at ~2.1 V, far below Cl- (~3.3 V).
comparison_and_interpretation.oxidation_limit_identical: Both oxidize first at 2.14 V via S2- -> LiS4 (polysulfide). Cl- is electrochemically inert until ~3.3 V (SCl) / ~3.4 V (PCl5, modelc only). Since S is present and is the VBM in both (S 3p), the oxidation onset is set by S, not Cl.
comparison_and_interpretation.consistency_with_electronic_structure: Fully consistent with the electronic/bonding inventory: S 3p is the VBM in BOTH (DOS/bands), ICOHP(P-S) -5.94 (comp1) vs -6.0 (modelc), ELF(P-S bridge) 0.946 vs 0.944. Same oxidation-susceptible species (S2-) and near-identical P-S covalency -> same oxidation onset.

quantitative_differences.more_inert_LiCl: modelc retains 1.6 LiCl vs comp1's 1.0 LiCl in the decomposition products — double the electrochemically inert halide fraction (LiCl stable to ~4 V).
quantitative_differences.milder_oxidation_extent: At the 2.14 V oxidation onset, modelc releases only 0.7 Li vs comp1's 1.75 Li — the oxidative decomposition EXTENT (Li capacity reacted) is ~2.5x smaller in modelc, even though the onset VOLTAGE is identical. modelc has less oxidizable S per formula (4.4 vs 5 S; 1 P vs 1 P) and more of the S is locked behind the stable Li3PS4 + LiCl assemblage.
quantitative_differences.high_voltage_Cl_chemistry: Only at >3.3 V does the higher Cl content of modelc manifest (SCl at 3.33 V, PCl5 at 3.39 V) — far above the operative S-limited window, so not relevant to practical stability.

comparison_and_interpretation.both_metastable_at_OCV: BOTH decompose at OCV (~1.72 V) to Li3PS4 + Li2S + LiCl with NO Li exchange — i.e. neither has a true thermodynamic stability plateau; the as-synthesized argyrodite is metastable. Practical stability is kinetic (sluggish decomposition). This is the well-known limitation of sulfide solid electrolytes (Zhu/He/Mo 2015).
comparison_and_interpretation.reduction_identical: Below ~1.7 V both reduce identically: P5+ -> P3-/P0 (Li3PS4 -> P -> LiP -> Li3P) and S2- stays as Li2S, plus LiCl. At Li-metal contact (0 V): Li3P + Li2S + LiCl (the known SEI). Cl-enrichment does not change reduction chemistry.

_LITERATURE_RECONCILIATION_2026_06_08_re._correction_note: REV2 (after reading the group's weekly report 2026-06-08): my first pass mischaracterized Zuo 2023 as 'Cl-rich simply worse'. The accurate, NUANCED finding is below. My grand-potential 'milder extent / more inert LiCl' result actually ALIGNS with the beneficial part of Zuo, not against it.

zuo_2023_FULL_PAPER_READ._paper: Zuo, Walther, Teo, Rueß, Wang, Rohnke, Schröder, Nazar, Janek (Janek group, Giessen + Nazar, Waterloo), Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202213228, 'Impact of the Chlorination of Lithium Argyrodites on the Electrolyte/Cathode Interface in Solid-State Batteries'. DOI 10.1002/anie.202213228. FULL PDF read 2026-06-08. NOTE their Cl-rich = Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 (LPSCl1.5); our modelc = Li5.4PS4.4Cl1.6 (close).
zuo_2023_FULL_PAPER_READ.their_decomposition_reactions: Eq(1) Li6PS5Cl -> LiCl + Li3PS4 + S + 2Li+ + 2e- (5e- per f.u. at full oxidation incl. Eq3). Eq(2) Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 -> 1.5 LiCl + Li3PS4 + 0.5 S + Li+ + e- (4e- per f.u.). Eq(3) Li3PS4 -> 0.5 P2S5 + 1.5 S + 3Li+ + 3e- (further oxidation). KEY: Cl-rich releases FEWER electrons/Li at first oxidation (1 vs 2) and makes MORE LiCl (1.5 vs 1.0).
zuo_2023_FULL_PAPER_READ.VALIDATES_our_grand_potential: Our 0-pressure ESW oxidation onset reactions REPRODUCE Zuo's Eq(1)/(2) almost exactly: comp1 -> Li3PS4 + LiCl + S(as 0.25 LiS4) + 1.75 Li (~Zuo Eq1's 2 Li + LiCl + Li3PS4 + S); modelc -> Li3PS4 + 1.6 LiCl + S(as 0.1 LiS4) + 0.7 Li (~Zuo Eq2's 1 Li + 1.5 LiCl + Li3PS4 + 0.5 S). Our 'modelc releases fewer Li (0.7 vs 1.75) and 2x more LiCl' = Zuo's electron count (1 vs 2 e-) and LiCl (1.5 vs 1.0). STRONG cross-validation of our grand-potential decomposition chemistry.

experiments.CV: Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5/C shows ~2x higher current density than Li6PS5Cl/C, maxima at the SAME potentials -> (a) Cl-rich MORE susceptible to electrochemical decomposition / lower oxidation onset, (b) oxidation MECHANISM is the same. Correlates with DSC/TGA: Cl-rich melt/crystallization shifts lower (523/493C vs 535/532C), mass loss onset 315C -> thermodynamically less stable.
experiments.interface_resistance_R_cat: vs NCM85, held 3.7 V: Li6PS5Cl steep sqrt(t) increase, rate const 13.2 Ohm*h^-0.5 ; Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 parabolic, rate const 8.9 Ohm*h^-0.5 -> Cl-rich interface degradation SLOWER.
experiments.cell_performance_NCM85: Initial charge/discharge: Li6PS5Cl 215/165 (CE 77%) ; Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 215/170 (CE 79%). After 50 cycles: 133 vs 145 mAh/g. Cl-rich BETTER.
experiments.ToF_SIMS_after_aging_3.7V_60h: S- and Cl- increase strongly for BOTH (decomposition). Oxygen-involving solid byproducts phosphate (PO2-/PO3-) and sulfate/sulfite (SO2-/SO3-): HIGHER for Li6PS5Cl, LOWER for Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5. Polysulfides (S4+S5+S6): HIGHER for Cl-rich. => Cl-rich forms LESS solid oxygenated (resistive) species, MORE gas/polysulfide.
experiments.DEMS_gas: O2 evolution similar (6.7 vs 6.8 umol/g_NCM, from NCM lattice at SOC>80%); Cl-rich evolves more SO2 gas.
experiments.mechanism_Fig7: < 4.2 V vs Li/Li+: electrochemical decomposition (delithiation) of the argyrodite dominates. >= 4.2 V vs Li/Li+: OXYGEN-INVOLVING degradation dominates (O2 released from NCM lattice reacts with the SE -> SO2 gas + solid sulfate/phosphate at interface). Cl-rich routes more to gas/polysulfide, less to solid sulfate/phosphate -> thinner/more-homogeneous Li-phosphate/sulfate layer -> lower R_int -> better cell.

zuo_2023_FULL_PAPER_READ.net_message: Cl-rich decomposes MORE easily (CV 2x, DSC/TGA less stable, lower onset) BUT its decomposition is MILDER in solid-resistive-byproduct terms (fewer electrons/Li released per f.u., more inert LiCl, more gas/polysulfide, less solid sulfate/phosphate) -> lower interface resistance growth (8.9 vs 13.2) -> BETTER cell performance (CE 79 vs 77, 50cyc 145 vs 133). NOT simply 'Cl-rich worse'.

_LITERATURE_RECONCILIATION_2026_06_08_re.our_interface_reactivity_calc_2026_06_08: tools/oxidation/interface_reactivity.py (pymatgen InterfacialReactivity, use_hull_energy, MP GGA_GGA+U). vs LiCoO2: comp1 min dE_rxn = -0.3227 eV/atom, modelc = -0.3308 (modelc +2.5% MORE reactive) -> matches Zuo CV 'Cl-rich decomposes more easily'. Products: both give the SAME solid OXYGENATED set Co9S8 + 0.1134 Li2SO4 (sulfate) + 0.2577 Li3PO4 (phosphate); modelc only trades 0.155 Li2S for 0.155 extra inert LiCl. vs carbon: BOTH 0.0 (C->C inert) -> Zuo's carbon-interface decomposition is electrochemical (bias-driven), NOT a chemical reaction. KEY LIMITATION (now precisely characterized by Zuo): the real divergence is that Cl-rich routes MORE to SO2 GAS + polysulfide and LESS to solid sulfate (SO_x) / phosphate (PO_x) [Zuo ToF-SIMS Fig4: PO2-/PO3-, SO2-/SO3- LOWER for Cl-rich]. Our closed SOLID-hull calc forces the SAME Li2SO4/Li3PO4 solids for both (no SO2 gas phase in MP, and the sulfate/phosphate need O from NCM = oxygen-involving >4.2V regime) -> it captures 'more reactive' but NOT the beneficial gas-diversion that lowers Cl-rich R_int. To model that one would need gas-phase (SO2/O2) chempots + the NCM O-release at >4.2V.
_LITERATURE_RECONCILIATION_2026_06_08_re.reading_of_our_extent_result_CORRECTED: Our grand-potential finding that modelc releases LESS Li at the oxidation onset (0.7 vs 1.75) and makes 2x more inert LiCl ALIGNS WITH the BENEFICIAL side of Zuo 2023 (milder / more-inert solid decomposition -> lower R_int -> better cell). My earlier (first-pass) claim that this 'is why the interface keeps decomposing / a disadvantage' was WRONG and is retracted.

gil_gonzalez_2022_FULL_PAPER_READ._paper: Gil-González, Ye, Wang, Shadike, Xu, Hu, Li (X. Li group, Harvard), Energy Storage Mater. 2022, 45, 484-493, 'Synergistic effects of chlorine substitution in sulfide electrolyte solid state battery'. DOI 10.1016/j.ensm.2021.12.008. FULL PDF + SI read 2026-06-08.
gil_gonzalez_2022_FULL_PAPER_READ.method_constrained_ensemble: CONSTRAINED-ENSEMBLE voltage window (NOT plain grand-potential). Eq(1): d_sD G' = (G_D - G_SE) + V*eps_RXN*K_eff, where (G_D - G_SE) = chemical grand-potential decomposition energy (same as our get_element_profile), and V*eps_RXN*K_eff = STRAIN penalty (V molar volume, eps_RXN = reaction volumetric strain = (V_products - V_SE)/V_SE, K_eff = effective bulk modulus = mechanical-constriction level). Solved by Fitzhugh et al. Lagrange minimization (Small 2019, 1901470) at K_eff = 0, 10, 20 GPa. A volume-EXPANDING decomposition (eps_RXN>0) is penalized under constriction -> raises decomposition energy -> stabilizes the SE -> WIDENS the window. AIMD: VASP PAW 300 eV, Gamma-only, NVT Nose-Hoover, 100 ps / 2 fs for conductivity.
gil_gonzalez_2022_FULL_PAPER_READ.phase_set_exclusions: They EXCLUDE LiS4 (mp-995393), SCl3 (mp-1186934), Li5PS4Cl2 (mp-1040450) from MP as non-physical / unlikely. OUR esw_grand_potential.py INCLUDED LiS4 (it appeared as '0.25 LiS4' at our 2.14 V onset). Excluding LiS4 should shift our oxidation onset UP toward their 2.40 V -> better 0-pressure agreement (TODO: add --exclude_phases).

their_numbers.LPSCl1.5_Keff0_stable_window_V: 1.70 - 2.40 V (Table S1). Just above 2.40 V: S + LiCl + P2S7 (Cl-bearing SCl/PCl3 appear at higher V). Below 1.70 V: P / LiP / Li3P + LiCl + Li2S (Cl-rich reduction route).
their_numbers.LPSCl1.5_Keff20_stable_window_V: 0.80 - 4.30 V (Table S1). Constriction widens ~+1.9 V anodic, ~-0.9 V cathodic. High-V products SCl4 + Li2PS3 + S (Cl-bearing, high molar volume = bigger strain penalty).
their_numbers.LPS_Cl_free_Keff20_anodic_limit_V: ~3.70 V (Table S2) — LOWER than LPSCl1.5's 4.30 V. => Cl-rich is MORE stabilized by constriction (its Cl-bearing decomposition products PCl3 / SCl / SCl4 have higher molar volume -> higher reaction strain -> bigger strain penalty).
their_numbers.experimental_windows_intro: LPSCl1.5 ~1.8 - 2.5 V; LPSCl1.0 (= Li6PS5Cl = comp1) ~1.3 - 2.3 V (their cells: 125 MPa formation + 38 MPa during test). Cl-rich window slightly higher / wider experimentally too.

gil_gonzalez_2022_FULL_PAPER_READ.validation_of_our_calc: Our grand-potential ESW (0 pressure): modelc OCV self-decomp 1.72 V, oxidation onset 2.14 V; comp1 the same. Gil-González K_eff=0 LPSCl1.5 stable window = 1.70 - 2.40 V. AGREEMENT IS EXCELLENT on the cathodic / OCV edge (1.72 vs 1.70) and good on the anodic edge (2.14 vs 2.40 — the 0.26 V gap is entirely the LiS4 inclusion). => our 0-pressure calc CORRECTLY reproduces the UNCONSTRICTED (K_eff=0) limit; the 'identical comp1 vs modelc onset' we found is the genuine 0-pressure physics, matching their flat 0-GPa curve (Fig 1a).
gil_gonzalez_2022_FULL_PAPER_READ.unified_picture: The Cl-rich oxidation-stability ADVANTAGE is a MECHANICAL-CONSTRICTION effect: at K_eff=0 the windows are similar across Cl (our calc + their 0 GPa), but under K_eff = 10 - 20 GPa the Cl-rich window widens MORE because Cl-bearing decomposition products (PCl3, SCl, SCl4) have larger molar volume -> larger reaction strain -> larger strain penalty -> stronger metastable stabilization. This UNIFIES Paper#1's mechanical and oxidation stories: the SAME volume / strain physics that governs elastic response gates the constrained electrochemical window.
gil_gonzalez_2022_FULL_PAPER_READ.reconciles_zuo_vs_gilgonzalez: Zuo 2023 (Cl-rich decomposes MORE easily, CV) and Gil-González 2022 (Cl-rich MORE stable under constriction) are NOT contradictory: the deciding variable is MECHANICAL CONSTRICTION K_eff. Weakly-constrained / intrinsic (Zuo CV, our K_eff=0): Cl-rich onset is equal-or-slightly-lower. Strongly-constrained (Gil-González 38 MPa cell -> high local K_eff at particle contacts): Cl-rich window widens more = more stable. Both captured by the K_eff axis.

wu_2026_calendar_aging_FULL_PAPER_READ._paper: Wu, Zhang, Wu, Xu, Zhou, H. Li, L. Chen, Fan Wu (IOP-CAS Beijing), Nano Energy 2026, 147, 111576, 'Calendar aging of sulfide all-solid-state batteries'. DOI 10.1016/j.nanoen.2025.111576. FULL PDF read 2026-06-08. THIS COMPLETES the oxidation-stability literature set.
wu_2026_calendar_aging_FULL_PAPER_READ.design: Calendar aging (open-circuit storage, 90 / 30 / -20 C, 5 days). Cathodes NCM811 vs LCO; SEs L6=Li6PS5Cl, L55=Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5, L53=Li5.3PS4.3Cl1.7; anodes Li vs LiIn; SOC 0 vs 100. Capacity retention before/after storage (Table 1).

Table1_retention_after_90C.NCM811/LiIn_100SOC: L6 68% > L53 59% > L55 48% (Cl-poor L6 BEST; Cl-rich worse).
Table1_retention_after_90C.NCM811/LiIn_0SOC: L6 98% > L55 93% > L53 88% (monotone: more Cl -> worse).
Table1_retention_after_90C.NCM811/Li_100SOC: L6 48% (Li metal much worse than LiIn 68% due to dead-Li + side reactions).
Table1_retention_after_90C.LCO/LiIn: L6 100SOC 92%, 0SOC 100% (LCO far more stable than NCM811: no H2-H3 / lattice-O release).

wu_2026_calendar_aging_FULL_PAPER_READ.key_findings: (1) Cl content: L6 (lowest Cl) has BEST calendar/thermal stability; Cl-rich (L55/L53) WORSE -> genuine Cl-rich penalty for shelf life. (2) SOC dominates: 100 SOC (charged) >> 0 SOC -> high SOC drives self-discharge parasitic electrode-electrolyte reactions. (3) Cathode: NCM811 H2-H3 transition >4.15 V releases lattice O -> accelerates degradation; LCO suppresses it (LCO 92% vs NCM811 68%); suppressing H3 improves retention >=21%. (4) Anode: Li metal worse than LiIn (dead Li). (5) XPS after 90C: PS4^3- -> polysulfides(-S0-)/SOx/POx/Li2S/Li3P; lattice-O & metal-oxide impurities appear.
wu_2026_calendar_aging_FULL_PAPER_READ.their_DFT_decomposition_consistent_with_: Their MP-based prediction (Table S1/Fig S5): NCM811-L6 interface decomposes at high T to Li2SO4, Li3PO4, polysulfides, NiO, Ni3S2, TM sulfides/oxides; self-decomposition -> polysulfides. CONSISTENT with our interface_reactivity vs LiCoO2 (Co9S8 + Li2SO4 + Li3PO4 + Li2S + LiCl) — same sulfate/phosphate/TM-sulfide chemistry.
wu_2026_calendar_aging_FULL_PAPER_READ.axis: THERMAL / CALENDAR (shelf life) axis — DISTINCT from the electrochemical-window (Gil-González) and interface-cycling (Zuo) axes. On THIS axis Cl-rich LOSES. Plus SOC and cathode (H3/lattice-O) are stronger levers than Cl content. Motivates O-doping (Paper#2) and cathode/anode choice.

MULTI_AXIS_CAPSTONE_oxidation_stability_._status: Oxidation-stability literature set COMPLETE (Gil-González 2022 + Zuo 2023 + Wu 2026, all full-text read 2026-06-08). The Cl-rich (modelc/LPSCl1.6) vs Cl-poor (comp1/Li6PS5Cl) 'stability' question is NOT one number — it is FOUR distinct axes, and Cl-rich wins on some, loses on others:
MULTI_AXIS_CAPSTONE_oxidation_stability_.axis_1_intrinsic_0pressure_window: DRAW. Our grand-potential ESW: oxidation onset ~identical (~2.1 V, S2--limited; S 3p VBM unchanged). Validated by Gil-González K_eff=0 (LPSCl1.5 1.70-2.40 V vs our 1.72-2.14). Cl does not move the bulk redox onset.
MULTI_AXIS_CAPSTONE_oxidation_stability_.axis_2_mechanically_constrained_window: Cl-rich WINS. Under K_eff=10-20 GPa the Cl-rich window widens MORE (Gil-González: LPSCl1.5 0.80-4.30 V vs Cl-free LPS 3.70 V) because Cl-bearing decomposition products (PCl3/SCl/SCl4) have higher molar volume -> bigger strain penalty. UNIFIES with our elastic/volume analysis (same strain physics).
MULTI_AXIS_CAPSTONE_oxidation_stability_.axis_3_cathode_interface_cycling: Cl-rich WINS (in cell). Zuo: Cl-rich decomposes more easily (CV 2x) BUT releases fewer e-/Li (Eq2 1 vs Eq1 2) + more inert LiCl + more SO2 gas/polysulfide + LESS solid sulfate/phosphate -> lower R_int growth (8.9 vs 13.2 Ohm h^-0.5) -> better cell (CE 79 vs 77, 50cyc 145 vs 133). Our grand-potential reproduces the fewer-Li/more-LiCl chemistry.
MULTI_AXIS_CAPSTONE_oxidation_stability_.axis_4_thermal_calendar_aging: Cl-rich LOSES. Wu 2026: 90C 5-day calendar retention NCM811/LiIn 100SOC L6 68% > L53 59% > L55 48% (more Cl -> worse shelf life). Also SOC (100>>0) and cathode (LCO>NCM811, H3/lattice-O) are STRONGER levers than Cl. Plus Cl-rich worse moisture stability (general). -> motivates O-doping (Paper#2).
MULTI_AXIS_CAPSTONE_oxidation_stability_.bottom_line: modelc (Cl-rich) gains conductivity (2.9->7.0 mS/cm) and, in a real constrained cell, equal-or-better oxidative interface behavior (axes 2,3); its genuine costs are calendar/thermal shelf life and moisture (axis 4). The intrinsic bulk redox onset is unchanged (axis 1, our calc). Do NOT say 'Cl-rich more/less oxidation-stable' without naming the axis.

comparison_and_interpretation.seminar_message_rev3: Paper#1 conductivity-vs-stability, FINAL framing (oxidation literature complete): the Cl-rich 'stability' answer is FOUR axes. (1) Intrinsic 0-pressure redox onset: DRAW (~2.1 V, S2--limited; our grand-potential = Gil-González K_eff=0). (2) Mechanically-constrained window: Cl-rich WINS (Gil-González K_eff=20: 0.80-4.30 V; Cl-products high molar volume -> strain stabilization -> unifies with our elastic story). (3) Cathode-interface cycling: Cl-rich WINS in-cell (Zuo: fewer e-/Li + more inert LiCl + gas diversion -> lower R_int -> better cell; our grand-potential reproduces the chemistry). (4) Calendar/thermal/moisture: Cl-rich LOSES (Wu: L6 68% > L55 48% at 100SOC/90C), and SOC+cathode are bigger levers. Headline: modelc's conductivity gain comes WITHOUT an oxidation-window penalty (axes 1-3 neutral-to-favorable); the real cost is shelf life/moisture -> the explicit motivation for Paper#2 O-doping. Never state a Cl-stability trend without naming the axis.

caveats: Closed-system SOLID-hull thermodynamics: NO gas phases (SO2/O2/Sx) -> cannot capture gas-evolution-driven interphase differences (Zuo's lower-R_int mechanism for Cl-rich).
0-pressure ESW only: the Cl-rich stability advantage is a mechanical-constriction (10-20 GPa) effect per Gil-González 2022 — needs a constrained-decomposition calc (TODO).

Intrinsic (bulk thermodynamic) ESW only — does NOT include electrochemical (bias-driven) interface decomposition; our InterfacialReactivity is CHEMICAL (zero-bias) only, hence carbon shows 0 reaction.

MP GGA_GGA+U energies; argyrodite ordered phase is ~tens meV/atom metastable in MP. The composition-based get_element_profile gives the window of the composition's hull-equilibrium assemblage (standard for non-MP / metastable phases).
modelc Li5.4PS4.4Cl1.6 treated as a composition (no MP entry, no MP-scale total energy of its own); window derived from MP hull phases at that composition — consistent with comp1's treatment.
